newsitem.title: USA: Agouron AIDS drug effective over 10 months.
newsitem.headline: Agouron AIDS drug effective over 10 months.

text.p: Agouron Pharmaceuticals Inc said Monday its Viracept AIDS drug in combination with AZT and 3TC continued to be an effective treatment over 10 months, the longest period for which results have been reported.

The company said that after 10 months, the three-drug combination kept HIV levels below the lower limit of sensitivity, while producing a continued rise in T-cell count. Previously, Agouron had reported successful results of the drug combination over a six month period.

Viracept is a protease inhibitor that was approved earlier this year by the Food and Drug Administration. Unlike some of the other protease inhibitors on the market, Agouron said Virarcept's most commonly observed adverse side effect was diarrhea.

Protease inhibitors are a cornerstone of virtually all aggressive AIDS treatments, and have been found to be highly effective when used in combination with 3TC and AZT, distributed by Glaxo Wellcome Plc.
Agouron reported its trial results on Monday at the Tenth International Conference on Anti-viral Research in Atlanta, the company said.
